faq.a: Abdulkarim is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ الْكَرِيم, whose core sense is abdulkarim; servant of the generous.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulkarim?
faq.a: Abdulkarim is associated with Arabic. Abdulkarim is Arabic عَبْدُ الْكَرِيم (ʿAbd al-Karīm), meaning 'servant of the Generous'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ الْكَرِيم is Arabic.
Abdulkarim can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdulkarim should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd al-Karīm is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdulkarim mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Abdulkarim is rendered عبدالکریم and carries the sense عبدالکریم، کریم کا بندہ.

faq.q: What does Abdulkarim mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdulkarim is rendered عبدالکریم and carries the sense عبدالکریم، بنده کریم.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-dul-ka-rim. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Abdulkarim?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Abdulkarim, abdulkarim. Script forms are عبدالكريم, عبدالکریم, عَبْدُ الْكَرِيم, अब्दुलकरीम.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
